tagline: A fully integrated geoscience company providing seismic and reservoir services to oil and gas and emerging new energy industries
hero_kpi_rationale: TGS, combined with PGS, positions the new group as a key player in seismic data processing via the cloud, a major technology wave. The majority of imaging work is now performed in the cloud, offering scalability and flexibility. This digital shift is the primary driver of future value.

kpis.name: Seismic imaging in the cloud
kpis.explanation: The majority of seismic data processing for TGS/PGS is now performed in the cloud, offering greater power and flexibility.
kpis.description: PGS indicates that most of its imaging work is now done in the cloud, which will apply to the merged TGS group. This improves scalability and access to resources.
kpis.signal: All imaging processing is cloud-based, a major digital transformation

kpis.name: Pre-funding ratio (MultiClient)
kpis.explanation: Percentage of MultiClient project costs covered by advance customer payments.
kpis.description: Pre-funding reached 140% of capitalized MultiClient investments, well above the 80-120% target, demonstrating strong customer confidence.
kpis.signal: Record pre-funding level, significantly above the 80-120% target

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross margin, reflecting the profitability of services provided.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved through better contract profitability and operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin is improving thanks to better contract execution and cost savings. Profitability on contract work is improving and approaching sustainable levels.
kpis.signal: Operating margin rising sharply, indicating cost discipline

kpis.name: Capital expenditures (capex)
kpis.explanation: Annual spending on physical assets and technology.
kpis.description: Capex is low because reliance on the cloud reduces the need for physical infrastructure.
kpis.signal: Reduced capex through digitalization and cloud adoption

kpis.name: Total workforce
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Headcount is declining slightly while productivity increases through digital tools.

kpis.name: New Energy revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated in emerging sectors such as offshore wind and carbon storage.
kpis.description: TGS/PGS completed its first offshore wind site characterization contract, won a major project extending well into 2024, and experienced strong customer interest in its ultra-high resolution 3D streamer solution.
kpis.signal: Quick start in new energy with triple-digit growth in 2023

kpis.name: Satellite data transmission
kpis.explanation: Use of satellites to transfer seismic data offshore in real time.
kpis.description: TGS/PGS has begun leveraging satellite technology to push the boundaries of offshore data transmission, improving the speed and reliability of operations.
kpis.signal: Key innovation to push the limits of offshore data transmission

risks.title: Decline in seismic demand linked to energy transition
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified in the impact matrix (Enterprise Level Risks) as: Accelerating energy transition and decline in demand for seismic. Direct and repeated language in CSRD/TCFD context. Trend stable but structural. High weight: ranked among the 3 priority material issues (Climate Change and Energy Transition).

risks.title: Major marine pollution incident or spill
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly listed in the impact matrix (Major spill or pollution incident). Intensive marine operations (fleet of seismic vessels). Direct language. Trend stable. High weight: linked to the material issue Biodiversity and Nature.

risks.title: Major cybersecurity incident affecting customer data
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified in the impact matrix (Victim of major cyber security incident). PGS manages high-value proprietary and multiclient seismic data. Direct language. Trend stable. Moderate-high weight: ranked among risks with enterprise value impact.

risks.title: Ability to attract and retain talent in a transitioning sector
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified in the impact matrix (Ability to attract, develop and retain talent). Context of energy transition and ongoing TGS merger. Direct language. Trend stable. High weight: ranked among the 3 priority material issues (Future Workforce).

risks.title: Risk of international sanctions violation or engagement in corrupt activities
risks.score_rationale: Risks explicitly listed in the impact matrix (Violation of international sanctions, Engagement in corrupt activities). Global operations in 40+ countries. Direct language. Trend stable. High weight: ranked among the 3 priority material issues (Business Ethics and Integrity).

risks.title: Dependence on proprietary technology and seismic innovation
risks.score_rationale: Implicit in the business model: GeoStreamer®, Ramform Titan-class, cloud-based Eos are critical assets. Indirect but repeated language (digitalization, innovation). Trend stable. Moderate weight: linked to competitiveness in a transitioning sector.

risks.title: Regulatory risk related to marine emissions and energy transition
risks.score_rationale: Implicit in references to EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, and net-zero 2050 targets. Direct language in compliance context. Trend up: new regulations mentioned (EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime MRV). Moderate-high weight: linked to Climate Change and Energy Transition.

risks.title: Risk of litigation or incident involving harm to marine fauna
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified in the impact matrix (Incident involving harm to marine fauna). Seismic operations in sensitive marine zones. Direct language. Trend stable. Moderate weight: linked to the material issue Biodiversity and Nature.

ai_positioning.summary: TGS does not develop generative AI in-house, but integrates advanced digital technologies (cloud, satellite) to improve the efficiency of its seismic services. Cloud-based processing opens the door to future AI applications.
evidence: The majority of seismic imaging is performed in the cloud
Use of satellites for offshore data transmission
Strong adoption of digital tools for operational efficiency
